note: Six frames. The web renders the desktop package, so the thread, gate, composer and review inherit docs/design-conformance/desktop-v2.json and are not repeated here; this inventory holds what the web draws of its own. The design describes a browser reached over Domovoi Cloud with account tiers. M1's web client runs over loopback and the tailnet with no relay and no accounts (S3.2, S0.6, Phase 2, Phase 5), so most of this design is blocked on the platform rather than unbuilt, and the finding is recorded once at the top: the Web v2 design is the Phase 2 product drawn early. Ruled 2026-09-18: this inventory is scoped to the limits page and what the web inherits from the desktop; the rest is not measurable until the relay exists, and five blocked out of eleven is the honest number.
sample: round trip 3.4s · 3 messages queued · the agent is unaffected
Webhooks get delivered twice when Stripe retries. Fix it properly, tests included.
Claim-then-commit is in, on a replay table keyed by event id. One spec still asserts the old at-least-once behaviour. Step 3 needs a migration on that machine, so I stopped and asked.
Also cover the claim-expiry case in replay.spec.ts

humanRead.note: the panel reports real browser state; whether its rows are the design's seven, with what, state and why, is not verified by this gate

The connect title and sub-line, the pair hint, the outcome cards and the five trust facts live in the design's data (connectTitle, connectSub, pairHint, outcomes, tailFacts), so the gate cannot hold them as drawn copy. Read them against the connect page.

The code is the daemon's word code (ND1), so the placeholder and the lock hint follow that shape instead of DVOI-XXXX-XXXX and 12 characters. Before pairing a tab knows only the address it dials, so the title names the host, not the daemon's machine name. The QR fill reads ?code= from the address bar and removes it. The daemon credential stays reachable one link down for a machine with no desktop.
